target_customer: Engineering teams running production AI agents
problem: Rules for agents live in long prompts and skills the agent may never open, so agents repeat mistakes already corrected.
business_model: Usage-based SaaS with a free tier and Growth plan at $299 a month plus $0.005 per turn
product_category: Runtime guidance infrastructure for AI agents

founders.name: Aryan Singhal
founders.background_notes: YC profile cites 4 papers on LLM failures; launch post says 6.

founders.name: Aditya Gupta
prior_employers: Multiple startups (computer vision and agent workflows, per launch post)
education: Purdue University, Computer Engineering (per YC page)

competitors.name: Invariant Labs
competitors.what: Policy over agent traces and tool calls

competitors.name: Lakera
competitors.traction_then: Part of Check Point since October 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Delivering rules at the right step with about 200 ms latency and measuring their effect across frameworks is standard infrastructure work with some hard evaluation parts.

defensibility.rationale: Stored rules and measurement history add lock-in, but frameworks and guardrail vendors can add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Guardrail rivals were being acquired by larger vendors by 2025 to 2026; no action against Mirrors recorded.

market_need_then: Teams add instruction after instruction to prompts after each failure; a launch write-up cites a design partner agent with 75 errors on one task despite a prompt rule.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical: guidance system for production agents

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared with other tools, including a different agent replay product, which causes confusion.

outcome_analysis: Mirrors joined YC in Fall 2026 and has only a launch article and a product site as evidence. It addresses a real pain for agent builders but sits in a crowded guardrail space where rivals have been acquired, so there is no outcome yet.
notes: No funding found beyond YC. Several search results describe a different product also called Mirrors (replay testing of agents); not clearly the same company, excluded. Competitor sources are undated vendor roundups.
